security_justification.trust_boundary: The delta describes the existing exchange-to-classifier boundary without changing peer trust, origin confinement, header forwarding or accepted inputs; no new principal, network endpoint or trust crossing is introduced.
security_justification.authority_provenance: Event identity and accepted acknowledgment matching retain their existing authoritative meaning; no contract authority, signed record or owner decision changes. This authored assessment and gates are technical evidence only, not human approval or activation.
security_justification.authentication_or_authorization: No authentication, credentials, origin restrictions, SDK authorization or deployment permission changes; the glossary and outcome-level clauses grant no access and leave the fetch adapter's governed authorization boundary untouched.
security_justification.audit_integrity: Exactly-one accepted acknowledgment for the same event remains the implemented acceptance rule. Explicit fully read response wording prevents another binding from confusing partial reads with malformed acknowledgments; event bytes, identity, integrity checks and current acceptance behavior are unchanged.
security_justification.confidentiality: Only specification and domain glossary text are added. No payload, header, credential or body is collected, stored, logged or transmitted differently, and the sink's existing secret-free outcomes remain untouched.
security_justification.mutation_ownership: The change owns exactly six proposal artifacts, one active delta and the Node CONTEXT glossary. Runtime sources, existing tests, adapter requirement and canonical specification are not written; #753 owns folding. Document assertions and evidence remain outside the repository.
security_justification.fail_posture: A failed body read still becomes timeout or transport_failure at the exchange, never acceptance. Malformed fully read 2xx outcomes remain protocol errors and sink failures; this clarification introduces no fallback, fail-open path or changed rejection behavior.
security_justification.error_disclosure: Classification codes and sink result mapping remain identical, with no new body, header, event data or native error exposed. Domain definitions describe outcomes without changing diagnostics, callbacks or exception handling.
security_justification.concurrency: No runtime code, in-flight tracking, promise coordination, scheduling or shared state changes. The classifier boundary is restated, not a new synchronization mechanism or ordering guarantee.
security_justification.lifecycle: No exchange deadline, SDK shutdown, sink closure or event lifecycle transition changes. Proposal precedes implementation; the active delta is not folded or archived here and technical verification grants no activation.
security_justification.resource_retention: Body bounds, socket cleanup, deadline coverage and in-flight resource ownership stay with existing runtime code and the unchanged adapter requirement. No retention policy or persistent store is added; verification evidence is external.
security_justification.retry_or_redelivery: Body-read failures already classify retryable through timeout or transport_failure, while malformed acknowledgments do not. The text removes ambiguity for a second binding without changing retry eligibility, budget, delay, attempt identity or byte-identical redelivery in the current implementation.
security_justification.cryptography: No cryptographic algorithms, hashes, signatures, key material or integrity-chain mechanisms change. A frozen upstream baseline identifies proposal ordering only; no new security claim or cryptographic assurance is inferred from it.
security_justification.privacy_transformation: No personal data, telemetry, event fields or transformation hooks are introduced or processed. Existing tests use synthetic fixtures and remain byte-identical; glossary concepts add no privacy collection or redaction behavior.
security_justification.external_security_integration: No collector, SIEM, exporter or external security service is added. The existing HTTP exchange and adapter remain unchanged, with no new integration or publication/deployment authorization from this specification clarification.
